scheme_name: Financial Assistance of Hearing Machine/Hearing Aid to Workers and their Dependents- Haryana Labour Welfare Board
description:
The Financial Assistance of Hearing Machine/Hearing Aid to Workers and their Dependents scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

This scheme was officially launched on February 1, 2018.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to workers and their dependents who are suffering from hearing impairments.

The scheme aims to improve the quality of life for individuals with hearing disabilities by enabling them to access hearing aids.

The specific goal is to ensure that at least 1,000 workers and their dependents benefit from this scheme annually.

The financial assistance under this scheme is set at a maximum of ₹10,000 for each eligible individual.

This amount is intended to cover the cost of hearing aids or machines that assist in hearing.

Eligible beneficiaries include registered workers under the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

Dependents of these registered workers can also apply for assistance under this scheme.

To qualify as a registered worker, an individual must be employed in any industry or establishment that falls under the purview of the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants.

Income criteria for eligibility stipulate that the monthly income of the worker should not exceed ₹15,000.

This income limit ensures that the benefits are directed towards economically weaker sections of society.

In terms of educational requirements, there are no specific educational qualifications mandated for applicants.

The application process is straightforward and involves several key steps.

Interested applicants must first obtain the application form from the Haryana Labour Welfare Board's official website or their local office.

The application form must be filled out completely with accurate personal and employment details.

Applicants are required to attach specific documents along with their application form.

These documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID.

Additionally, applicants must provide proof of employment which can be in the form of a salary slip or employment certificate.

Medical certification confirming the hearing impairment is also necessary.

This medical certificate should be issued by a recognized medical practitioner or hospital.

Once the application form and documents are ready, they must be submitted to the local Haryana Labour Welfare Board office.

The application can also be submitted online through the Haryana Labour Welfare Board's official portal.

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the concerned authorities.

The review process typically takes about 30 days from the date of application submission.

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the applicant.

Disbursement of funds is usually completed within 15 days after approval.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board is the implementing authority for this scheme.

The Board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment, Haryana.

For any inquiries or assistance, applicants can contact the Haryana Labour Welfare Board at their official helpline number.

The helpline number is 1800 180 2080.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Haryana government to enhance the welfare of workers and their families.

This initiative reflects the government's commitment to inclusivity and support for individuals with disabilities.

Statistical data shows that hearing impairment is a significant issue affecting a large number of individuals in Haryana.

According to the 2011 Census, around 1.5% of the population in Haryana has some form of hearing disability.

This translates to approximately 1.5 million people who may benefit from such welfare schemes.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board has been proactive in identifying and addressing the needs of these individuals.

The scheme is not only about providing financial assistance but also about raising awareness regarding hearing disabilities.

By facilitating access to hearing aids, the scheme aims to promote better communication and social integration for affected individuals.

The Haryana government has allocated a budget of ₹2 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2023-2024.

This budget allocation is expected to cover the costs for approximately 2,000 beneficiaries.

The scheme is reviewed periodically to assess its impact and effectiveness.

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the scheme further.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board also collaborates with various NGOs and health organizations to promote this scheme.

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform workers about the availability of this assistance.

These campaigns include workshops and seminars aimed at educating workers about hearing impairments and available support.

The scheme is part of the larger framework of social security measures implemented by the Haryana government.

It aligns with the national policies aimed at empowering persons with disabilities.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is non-repayable.

This means that beneficiaries do not have to pay back the amount received for the hearing aids.

The scheme is designed to be user-friendly and accessible to all eligible individuals.

In conclusion, the Financial Assistance of Hearing Machine/Hearing Aid to Workers and their Dependents scheme is a vital initiative by the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

It aims to enhance the quality of life for workers and their dependents suffering from hearing impairments.

By providing financial assistance, the scheme ensures that individuals can access necessary hearing aids.

This initiative reflects the commitment of the Haryana government to support vulnerable populations.

The scheme is a significant step towards inclusivity and empowerment of individuals with disabilities in the state.
